source: Db35MX-A_mA.mp4 (1080x1920, 60 fps container with 24 fps content, 88.96 s)
style: 3D animated (Pixar-style CG) for 0-86.00 s; black frame 86.00-86.12 s; live-action handheld phone 'real me' flex tag 86.12-88.96 s (15 shots). White bold uppercase word-by-word captions with black outline, lower-middle of frame.
logline: A teen's dad sells his whole resale stock for $200 and kicks him out for 'failing'; he rebuilds from one pair of AirPods to a warehouse business, the parents come to apologise, and he makes Dad say 'I was wrong' twice - then reminds him he still owes $1,800.

hook.mechanic: Cold open mid-argument with an injustice the viewer instantly feels: 'You sold all my stuff?' / 'Yep.' / '200 bucks' over a smug Dad ECU, a whip-pan to the empty TV wall, a snap zoom on the son's '200?!', then 15 flash-insert shots (0.08-0.4 s) of the sold stuff being hauled away; hook title 'DAD SAID I'D FAIL' frames the payoff.
hook.first_line: You sold all my stuff? / Yep.

montage.description: Grind-to-scale montage (sparse V.O. and reaction lines, music-driven): kneels in a dark room and opens a laptop, near-empty balance, lists AirPods, buyer message 'Is this still available?' -> 'Yes', bag, label printer, parcel, payment, 'My first sale', rising chart, time-lapse stacks growing from the floor; cross-cut to Dad on the porch at dusk watching through the window ('He's actually doing it?'); '500 orders?' -> 'Bro!' jump; then a fast scale run with whip-blur transitions: tape gun, walls of AirPods boxes growing, packing, labels, hand-off to a courier, orders app, wink, tracking past pallets. Ends on the symmetrical 'It actually worked' warehouse shot (64.47 s).

stats.dead_air: None in the audio sense: music runs the full reel (silencedetect at -35 dB/0.4 s found no silence). Gaps with no dialogue (>= 1.5 s): 24.26-26.98 (2.7 s), 39.54-42.45 (2.9 s), 43.05-46.70 (3.7 s), 47.62-54.00 (6.4 s), 60.00-64.62 (4.6 s), 70.08-72.04 (2.0 s), 85.90-88.96 (3.1 s).

beats.summary: HOOK: 'You sold all my stuff?' 'Yep.' '200 bucks.' Snap zoom '200?!' then a flash-insert burst of the sold stuff being hauled off.
Escalation: Mom walks in; Dad: 'He wasn't making any money... You already failed.' Close-up on the son taking it.
Eviction, one continuous take: 'This isn't a real job.' 'Not in my house... Get out.' Son turns to Mom.
Exit and vow: rapid packing inserts, walks past his parents, ECU 'When this works, don't say you believed in me.' Rainy night walk, memory echo, 'Watch me.'
Grind: laptop in the dark, lists AirPods, first buyer, ship, 'My first sale.', chart rises.
Growth seen: stacks grow; Dad on the porch sees him through the window ('He's actually doing it?'); '500 orders?' 'Bro!'
Scale montage into a warehouse; 'It actually worked.'
Parents find out: Mom on her phone, 'Look.' Dad: 'No way.' 'You said he'd fail?'
Payoff: parents at his door; 'I was wrong.' 'Say it louder.' 'I'm proud of you.' Twist: 'So you still owe me $1,800.'
Topper: phone shows '*10,000 ORDERS*'; 'Wait. What?!' snap ECU, cut to black.
Real-me tag: handheld live-action flexes (friends, stock room, cars, jet, yacht, jet ski) at 0.1 s per shot; loops.

transcription: faster-whisper 'small' (CPU, int8), word timestamps; checked line by line against the burned-in word captions. 'My' (first sale) and Dad's 'Wait.' at 54 s come from captions only; 'About what? / I saw what you built.' are whisper only (no captions shown). Speakers assigned from lip movement and framing.
why_it_works: Injustice in the first second: a smug one-word 'Yep.' and '200 bucks' make the viewer take the son's side before any setup; the hook title 'DAD SAID I'D FAIL' promises the payback.
Comic punctuation through camera: snap zooms and a whip-pan to the empty TV wall turn each line into a beat; reaction ECUs are cartoon-big (saucer eyes, giant jaw).
The flash-insert burst (15 shots in 2.7 s) under 'That cost me 2,000' makes the loss concrete and the pace frantic without new dialogue.
The eviction plays as one 10.6 s continuous take with an arc and whip-pan, so the fight feels real and the long shot contrasts with the hyper-cut hook.
A quotable vow straight into the lens ('When this works, don't say you believed in me') and a lonely rain walk set up the arc in classic underdog grammar.
Grind montage makes the method feel achievable (laptop, list one item, 'Is this still available?', ship, first sale) - perfect for a reseller audience and the 'Comment AI' CTA.
Cross-cutting Dad watching through the window lets the antagonist witness the rise before the confrontation, so the apology lands.
Payoff milks the win ('Say it louder') then flips to a money joke ($1,800) and tops it with '*10,000 ORDERS*' - three escalating buttons in 8 s.
Cut to black then a 0.1 s-per-shot real-life flex montage ties the cartoon fable to the creator's actual life and loops back to the start.
undetermined: Music not identified (music bed under the whole reel; only speech transcribed).
Flash-insert burst 3.88-6.55 s: AI morph frames between inserts were folded into neighbouring shots; any image held for 2+ content frames counted as a shot, so the count there is approximate (+/- 2).
14.22-24.83 s judged one continuous take (frame differences stay smooth through the arc and whip-pan); a hidden cut inside the 22.0 s whip cannot be fully ruled out.
29.62-33.25 s: the parents' memory overlay is treated as an in-shot dissolve, not a cut.
Speakers of 'You gonna let him kick me out?' (son, inferred) and 'You said he'd fail?' (Mom, inferred) are not certain.
'Started.' at 11.94 s is probably '(I just) started'; 'About what?' and 'I saw what you built.' are whisper only, without captions.
Dad's 'Wait.' at ~54.0 s and 'My' in 'My first sale' are caption only; their timings are estimated.
Buyer/delivery figure in shot 9 is not clearly identified.
